overview.description: Complete reference for agent configuration file format

fields.field: The name of the agent (optional, derived from filename if not specified).
The MCP servers the agent has access to.
The tools available to the agent.
Tool name remapping for handling naming collisions.
Tools that can be used without prompting.
Commands run at specific trigger points.
Whether to include MCP servers from mcp.json files.
The model ID to use for this agent.
Keyboard shortcut for quickly switching to this agent.
Message displayed when switching to this agent.

fieldDef.name: name
fieldDef.description: Specifies the name of the agent. Used for identification and display purposes.

fieldDef.name: description
fieldDef.description: Provides a description of what the agent does. Primarily for human readability.
fieldDef.example: { "description": "An agent specialized for AWS infrastructure tasks" }

fieldDef.name: prompt
fieldDef.description: High-level context for the agent, similar to a system prompt. Supports inline text and file:// URIs.

variant.example: { "prompt": "You are an expert AWS infrastructure specialist" }

pathResolution.rule: Resolved relative to the agent configuration file's directory. file://./prompt.md → prompt.md in the same directory as the agent config file://../shared/prompt.md → prompt.md in a parent directory

fieldDef.name: mcpServers
fieldDef.description: Specifies which MCP servers the agent has access to. Each server is defined with a command and optional arguments.

serverFields.serverField: The command to execute to start the MCP server.
Arguments to pass to the command.
Environment variables to set for the server.
Timeout for each MCP request in milliseconds. Default: 120000.

OAuth configuration for HTTP-based MCP servers.
Pre-registered OAuth client ID. Fallback when Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) fails. Required for services like Slack, GitHub, Figma that don't support DCR. Custom redirect URI for OAuth flow. Example: "127.0.0.1:7778" Array of OAuth scopes to request. Example: ["read", "write"]. Use empty array [] to bypass scope requirements.

fieldDef.name: tools
fieldDef.description: Lists all tools the agent can potentially use. Includes built-in tools and MCP server tools.

syntax.rule: Built-in tools: specified by name, e.g. "read", "shell"

fieldDef.name: toolAliases
fieldDef.description: Advanced feature to remap tool names. Used to resolve naming collisions between MCP servers or create intuitive names. Key = original tool name (with server prefix for MCP tools), value = new name.

fieldDef.name: allowedTools
fieldDef.description: Tools that can be used without prompting the user for permission. Does NOT support bare "*" wildcard. Supports glob-style patterns.

patternType.label: Wildcard — any tool from pattern servers

patternTypes.patternType: "@git-*/*" matches any tool from git-* servers

patternRules.rule: * matches any sequence of characters (including none)
Exact matches take precedence over patterns
Server-level permissions (@server_name) allow all tools from that server
"*" wildcard NOT supported (unlike the tools field)

fieldDef.securityNote: When write tools (write, shell, or MCP tools with write access) are allowed, the agent can modify any file the tools have access to, including all resources under ~/.kiro.

fieldDef.name: toolsSettings
fieldDef.description: Configuration for specific tools. Specifications that configure allowable patterns are overridden if the tool is also in allowedTools.

fieldDef.name: resources
fieldDef.description: Gives the agent access to local resources: files, skills, or knowledge bases.

resourceTypes.resourceType: Loaded directly into context at startup. Use for content the agent always needs.
Metadata (name + description) loaded at startup; full content loaded on demand. Skill files must begin with YAML frontmatter containing name and description.
Indexed documentation for semantic search. Supports millions of tokens with incremental loading.

fieldDef.pathSupport: Specific paths, glob patterns, absolute or relative paths.

knowledgeBaseFields.kbField: Path to index. Use file:// prefix for local paths.
Display name for the knowledge base.
Indexing strategy: "best" (default, higher quality) or "fast" (quicker indexing).
Re-index when agent spawns. Default: false.

fieldDef.name: hooks
fieldDef.description: Commands run at specific trigger points during agent lifecycle and tool execution.

hookTypes.hookType: Triggered when the agent is initialized.
Triggered when the user submits a message.
Triggered before a tool is executed. Can block the tool use.
Triggered after a tool is executed.
Triggered when the assistant finishes responding.

hookFields.hookField: Pattern to match tool names for preToolUse and postToolUse. Uses internal tool names (fs_read, fs_write, execute_bash, use_aws) not simplified names.

fieldDef.name: includeMcpJson
fieldDef.description: Whether to include MCP servers defined in mcp.json files (~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json for global, <cwd>/.kiro/settings/mcp.json for workspace). When true, agent has access to all MCP servers from those files in addition to those in mcpServers.
fieldDef.note: The only valid field name is includeMcpJson. The field useLegacyMcpJson is NOT valid and is silently ignored.

fieldDef.name: model
fieldDef.description: The model ID to use for this agent. Must match an available model from the Kiro CLI model service. Check available models with /model command. Falls back to default model with a warning if unavailable.

fieldDef.name: keyboardShortcut
fieldDef.description: Keyboard shortcut for quickly switching to this agent during a chat session.

behavior.rule: Pressing the shortcut switches to this agent.
Pressing again while on this agent switches back to the previous agent.
Conflicting shortcuts are disabled with a warning. Use /agent swap to switch manually.

fieldDef.name: welcomeMessage
fieldDef.description: Message displayed when switching to this agent. Appears after the agent switch confirmation.
fieldDef.example: { "welcomeMessage": "What would you like to build today?" }

fileLocations.location: Project-specific agents. Only available when running Kiro CLI from that directory or subdirectories. Share with team via version control.
User-wide agents. Available from any directory.
fileLocations.precedence: Local agents take precedence over global agents with the same name (warning is logged).

bestPractices.practice: Start restrictive: begin with minimal tool access and expand as needed.
Name clearly: use descriptive names that indicate the agent's purpose.
Document usage: add clear descriptions to help team members understand the agent.
Version control: store agent configurations in your project repository.
Test thoroughly: verify tool permissions work as expected before sharing.
Use local agents for project-specific configs, global agents for general-purpose use.
Review allowedTools carefully. Use specific patterns over wildcards.
Configure toolsSettings.write.allowedPaths to restrict write operations to specific paths.
Use preToolUse hooks to audit or block sensitive operations.
